QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Performance and Benchmarking_6

question.text: Kaveri Growth AIF drew INR 100 crore at t=0, paid INR 5 crore of fees and expenses at end of each of Y1 through Y4 (paid out-of-pocket at the fund), and distributed INR 180 crore at end of Y5 (net of all fees/carry/tax). The approximate Net IRR at the investor level is:

explanation.text: The Logic: Investor cash flows: -100 at t0, -5 each at t1..t4, +180 at t5. Solve XIRR so the NPV of all flows equals zero. Iterating around 9-10%: the discounted sum of the four -5 fee outflows plus +180 at t5 against -100 at t0 balances near IRR ≈ 9.16%, with 9.5% being the closest listed option. Net IRR uses investor-level cash flows including fund expenses, management fees, incentive fees, taxes, and timing of every cash flow. The Trap: 7.5% underestimates; 12.5% ignores the intermediate fee drag; 15% is close to a Gross IRR that excludes fee outflows. Note: Per the workbook, Net IRR must include all fee, expense, carry, and tax outflows at the investor level — 9.5% is selected as the closest option to the calculated ~9.16%.
